user.title: Tempem BLE
user.description: Tempem beacons heard by Home Assistant's Bluetooth (local adapter, ESPHome Bluetooth proxies or a remote gateway) are discovered automatically. You can also pick one by hand, or add a remote gateway for a site on another network.

menu_options.pick_sensor: Add a Tempem sensor that Home Assistant can hear
menu_options.gateway: Add a remote gateway (ESP32 posting over the internet)

gateway.title: Remote gateway
gateway.description: A remote gateway is an ESP32-C6 running the Tempem gateway firmware (installable from the browser, see the integration's documentation) at a site that cannot reach Home Assistant's local network. It posts the beacons it hears to a webhook on your public Home Assistant URL (e.g. through a Cloudflare Tunnel).

gateway_url.title: Webhook URL
gateway_url.description:
Paste this URL into **Webhook URL** on the gateway's web page (the browser installer's **Visit device** button opens it):

`{webhook_url}`

Treat it like a password: anyone who knows it can post readings. You can see it again later under this entry's **Configure** button. If the URL does not start with your public domain, set **Settings → System → Network → Home Assistant URL → Internet**.

abort.already_in_progress: Configuration for this device is already in progress.
abort.no_devices_found: No Tempem sensors are being heard right now. Make sure the Bluetooth integration is set up and the sensor is in range.
abort.not_supported: This device is not a Tempem/Dusun temperature beacon.

init.title: Battery polling
init.description: The battery level is not broadcast; it is read by connecting to the sensor. Connecting costs the sensor some battery, so keep this infrequent. Set to 0 to never connect. Sensors behind a remote gateway are polled by the gateway itself.
